text:
Rep. Jon Dunwell shares support for local candidates and recaps Newton City Council activity
N. J. Kirk
Rep. Jon Dunwell, a member of the Iowa House of Representatives, shared several updates on his Twitter account in July 2026, highlighting local political events and expressing support for candidates in upcoming elections.
On July 20, Dunwell promoted an event hosted by Ashley Hinson, writing: "Looking forward to Ashley's BBQ Bash on August 29th! Good food, great people, and a chance to stand with a leader who fights for Iowa. We need Ashley Hinson in the US Senate. Hope to see you there."
The following day, Dunwell recapped activities at a recent city council meeting, "Last night was a long one at Newton City Council. The evening started with a work session on Franchise Fees, rolled into the regular Council meeting, and wrapped up with another work session on the Site Plan Review process. The public hearing on the 2nd reading of the Franchise" (July 21).
Later that morning, Dunwell contrasted two political campaigns in Iowa, "Rob Sand’s campaign is photo ops at Casey’s, staged townhalls, and a highlight reel. Zach Lahn’s campaign is a vision: an Iowa government focused on the people who live here, not special interests and lobbyists. A sixth-generation Iowan. A farmer and businessman who answers to" (July 21).
Ashley Hinson is currently serving as U.S. Representative for Iowa's 2nd congressional district and has announced her candidacy for U.S. Senate in 2026.
Rob Sand is the State Auditor of Iowa known for his focus on government accountability.
Zach Lahn is running for statewide office emphasizing transparency and service to Iowans over special interests.
Franchise fees are charges levied by municipalities on utility companies operating within city limits; discussions about these fees often arise during city council meetings such as those held in Newton.
